$comment: Named, expiring waivers for docs:check check 2 (GENERATED blocks).
This exists for exactly one situation: a GENERATED block whose oracle lives in ANOTHER
live lane's in-flight work, so no checkout that can see the failure is able to fix it.
Regenerating from the wrong checkout would bake that lane's unshipped state into dev.
It is deliberately NOT a general 'cross-lane' escape hatch. A self-declared exemption on
lane:ship would let any lane that finds the docs guard inconvenient switch it off. So a
waiver must name the exact file and block, name the owning lane, and carry an expiry.
Every other docs:check failure still blocks, including other GENERATED blocks.
- A waiver suppresses the failure and prints a WAIVED line. It never hides it.
- Past `expires`, the waiver stops suppressing and the gate goes red, loudly, so
somebody looks at it. Extending an expiry is a decision someone has to make on
purpose; it is not the default.
- `--fix` ignores waivers entirely: if you can regenerate, regenerate.
- DELETE the entry when the owning lane lands and regenerates the block. A waiver that
outlives its cause is worse than no waiver.
